label: correctness relative to supplied reference maps
term: correctness relative to supplied reference maps
definition: Correct g t means g.content t = g.condition (g.referent t). The reference map is supplied independently of this equality, so a fixed referent can coexist with error. A nondiscriminating condition can make different referents equally correct. This does not establish underdetermination under rich individuating contents.
